top_story.headline: Pentagon gave Marriott a no-bid deal to house 600 attendees at a Secretary of War conference, posted after the event ended
top_story.dek: The sole-source justification and award notice for the September 29 to October 1 Washington conference both went public on October 13.
paragraphs: Washington Headquarters Services, part of the Department of Defense, awarded a sole-source contract to Marriott Hotel Services Inc. (spelled "Marriot" in the justification) for lodging and catering for 600 government attendees. They were attending a conference hosted by the Office of the Secretary of War at a single hotel in the Washington area. Check-in was September 29, 2026 and check-out October 1. The justification is dated September 21. The award notice lists $724,742, signed September 25. Both were posted October 13, after the stay was over. The justification itself redacts the dollar value and says only that it covers a three-day period of performance. It lists Marriott's address as 901 Massachusetts Avenue NW and says the contract will use Official Representation funds.

The agency's stated reason for not competing is that major Washington venues were already booked. It cites "pre-existing citywide bookings, recurring annual international summits, and large-scale national conventions," and says no other property could meet scale, schedule and security at once. It describes its market research as "cold calls" to high-capacity hotels. According to the document, all 600 people had to be housed "under one roof" for "operational security, force protection, and strict scheduling synchronization." The hotel also had to provide a dedicated, secure space for uniform distribution during attendee in-processing. The action was done as a simplified-procedures commercial-item sole source under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul, citing 41 U.S.C. 1901.

sections.headline: Today's Top Story is a sole-source justification; the only other new one is a routine currency-press parts buy

sections.headline: Argonne's Equinox AI supercomputer solicitation is tied to the Genesis Mission executive order
paragraphs: Five new solicitations and 115 repeats left out. The two cards come from documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: Argonne National Laboratory seeks an AI supercomputer for the Genesis Mission
meta: Department of Energy (Argonne National Laboratory, operated by UChicago Argonne, LLC)
blocks.text: The request for proposals for the "Equinox" AI system asks for a rack-scale computing environment with a 16-rack base system and room to expand. According to the statement of work, "the system will provide compute resources in support of the Genesis Mission, established through Executive Order 14363, 'Launching the Genesis Mission.'" Argonne's cover letter says current planning is a conventional purchase "with LTO financing used, as appropriate" (lease-to-ownership), and Addendum 2 says non-U.S. citizens face Foreign National Access Program approval that "may take up to forty-five (45) business days, or longer." Notice posted earlier; addendum and statement of work read today.

blocks.title: Navy plans to build child development centers through an Other Transaction agreement that could lead to a no-compete production deal
meta: Department of the Navy (Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Atlantic)
blocks.text: The area-of-interest notice seeks industrialized-construction vendors for Navy child development centers under Other Transaction Authority (10 U.S.C. § 2808a). The notice warns that any agreement awarded "may result in the award of a follow-on production OT agreement or contract without the use of further competitive procedures." Document read today on a notice posted earlier.

sections.headline: Marine special operations medical training contract drops classified-facility requirements
paragraphs: Two new combined synopsis/solicitations and 1,507 repeats left out. The cards below come from documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: Marine special operations medical training contract drops its clearance requirements
meta: Department of Defense (Marine Forces Special Operations Command)
blocks.text: An amendment to the Special Operations Medical Training Services indefinite-delivery contract solicitation says: "The purpose of this amendment is to remove the DD254 and FCL requirements. Section L & M have been updated accordingly." The DD254 is the form specifying classified-facility security needs, and FCL means facility clearance. The amendment was posted September 16.

sections.headline: No new special notices, but documents read today turned up NASA space-station requirements and Navy Aegis overhaul work
paragraphs: Zero new special notices; 44 repeats left out. The items below come from documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: NASA releases technical requirements for commercial space stations
meta: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (Johnson Space Center)
blocks.text: A technical-library data drop for the Commercial Low Earth Orbit Destination contract says NASA "seeks to purchase end-to-end services from a commercial service provider," including crew and cargo transportation. It requires the systems to be "two failure tolerant to catastrophic hazards and for a controlled Destination Deorbit." Another requirement says an unpiloted visiting spacecraft must autonomously abort its approach if its communications link to the station is lost. The file was posted October 9.

blocks.title: Navy plans overhaul of Aegis fire-control components, including equipment used for allied navies
meta: Department of the Navy (Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane)
blocks.text: A draft statement of work covers overhaul and repair of the SPG-62 antenna and MK82 gun and guided-missile director. It says the MK99 fire control system "is the illuminator for the Aegis Weapons System and used in support of United States Navy (USN) and Foreign Military Sales (FMS)." It also says personnel "will require up to a SECRET clearance."

blocks.title: Army industry day for Winfield Locks and Dam rehabilitation cites active cracking in gate anchorages
blocks.text: The industry-day presentation lists a "critical safety need": full replacement of the post-tensioned anchorage system "due to active Stress Corrosion Cracking." It says the work can be done concurrently with main lock outages.

items: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration — white-paper request for commercial multi-constellation satellite operations, using Other Transaction Authority (2027-NESDIS-BB-0001).
Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security — NATO request for information on a tactical voice and data gateway linking allied radios that use different encryption (MS-424396-ANCONTOR).

sections.headline: Energy Department asks industry to recover critical minerals from legacy nuclear weapons sites
paragraphs: Two new sources-sought notices and 93 repeats left out. Most of the items below come from documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: Energy Department offers aluminum, copper, lithium hydride and uranium mill tailings for commercial recovery
meta: Department of Energy (Office of Environmental Management)
blocks.text: The expression-of-interest documents say about 8,000 tons of aluminum and 2,000 tons of copper sit in legacy inventories at the Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant site in Kentucky, and about 12,000 pounds of lithium hydride at the Oak Ridge Reservation. They also describe about 16.2 million tons of uranium mill tailings at the Moab Crescent Junction disposal cell, which "contain multiple co-located critical minerals." The material was posted September 30.

blocks.title: Defense Information Systems Agency plans to move electromagnetic spectrum IT onto the Maven Smart System
meta: Department of Defense (Defense Information Systems Agency)
blocks.text: The draft performance work statement says the effort "will transition legacy spectrum management, situational awareness, command and control, and training capabilities into a unified, cloud-native, AI-assisted ecosystem on the Maven Smart System." It calls for using large language models to extract data from unstructured PDF records. To avoid conflicts of interest, support contractors "will not perform hands-on platform coding."

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs market research on enterprise software waives the FedRAMP certification requirement
meta: Department of Veterans Affairs (Technology Acquisition Center)
blocks.text: The request for information covers enterprise solutions for productivity and collaboration, security and compliance, case management and low-code development. It says that under a July 28, 2026 policy memo, "this RFI does not require respondents' alternatives to hold existing FedRAMP certification to be considered."

items: Federal Emergency Management Agency — sources sought for a senior executive aircraft lease; the performance work statement is attached. sections.headline: A $2.2 billion Navy award to TOTE Services, signed in July, surfaces in the Pentagon's delayed data
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

36 new awards of $2 million or more, all of them Department of Defense awards signed July 13 and just published after the department's 90-day data hold. No large modifications this run, and 1 cut, which was routine. The 28 routine ones, cut included, are listed with links in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: TOTE Services, LLC received $2,206,000,000 obligated from the Department of the Navy for an award classified as combat ships and landing vessels, under the ship building and repair industry code.
